how: The starter invites help and accepts another member's proposal without an evidenced appointment.
Members are asked to complete the face and later to save it under attack.
A direct reply reports adding a blue pixel and asks for nothing back.
Participants revise lettering into a smaller face and change template colors to resemble the skin.
Builders report continuing letters, placing the first square and adding a blue pixel.
Members request coordinates and locate both the rebuilt and finished face.
Inability to control existing space is an explicit reason to reject expansion.
Members call for rescue and urge holding the remaining face.
Participants alter the border and face color while limiting growth to what they can hold.
A loss report names the Netherlands as destroyer, supporting participant attribution rather than independently verified identification.
A shift is explicitly limited to avoid provoking the neighbouring group.
Reported neighbour expansion enters internal border deliberation and prompts explicit acceptance of keeping black.
A participant says moving elsewhere is necessary and reports starting a new face.
Another participant selects a new location after saying another move seems necessary.
An appeal asks the face's builders to help another work without documenting their response.
Completion declarations credit contributors and later describe the surviving mark as a modest success.
A participant records a swastika appearing and disappearing on the neighbouring face.
A participant mourns the face's attributed destruction during the event.
A fake episode fools readers and receives an explicit April Fools explanation.
A request for scripts is visible but does not establish that anyone deployed them.
Visible agreement and a report from unseen chats cannot establish whether decided order existed across the whole effort.
Carrying an imported plan does not establish acting as a representative toward another room.
Borrowing a neighbouring plan and celebrating nearby marks leave coalition membership unobserved.
A final location under FTL does not establish residence under a host's rule.
The fake-video explanation provides no evidence of rules containing canvas discussion.
Closing congratulations do not show a decision to continue the effort elsewhere.
Defensive recruitment and a report of someone altering Doc leave an offensive call by this room unobserved.
Attributed destruction and mourning do not establish an ongoing exchange of taunts with a rival.
Naming a destroyer does not establish a quarrel predating the canvas.
Jokes about an orange tan do not establish inherited lore, ideology or loyalty to a color.
Attributing a loss to the Netherlands does not establish a prior tie motivating an attack by this room.
The reported neighbour preference does not show a dispute over who can commit the room.
The post-event orange joke does not establish a dispute over editing or authoring the preserved canvas.
The opening request receives direct replies reporting continued letters and a contributed pixel.
The edited opening combines recruitment and revised design without preserving a separately timed start followed by a call.
Building already encounters erosion of partial letters before later explicit defence, fitting upkeep of partial rather than necessarily completed work.
Defensive border discussion anticipates neighbour expansion but does not establish subsequent direct negotiations.
Avoiding provocation is explicit but a prior settled agreement causing that restraint is not evidenced.
Strain elicits a script request while the proposed endpoint of actual machine placement remains unobserved.
Completion is marked directly by saying they did it and congratulating contributors.
Celebration precedes some fate reports but no cited passage makes celebration the cause of recording or preservation.
A loss report and closing evaluation do not show a transition into a continuing project.
Scarcity leads to moving only when relinquishing the threatened spot is chosen, since limited control can instead justify restricted defence.
Template edits and an accepted design proposal do not preserve an order proving that posting the template settled the discussion.
The opening call receives a bare report of adding a blue pixel without establishing obligations for every reader or responses through silent placement.
An appeal for another work and an imported plan do not establish that defensive shortage produced exchanged help.
The help appeal and reported FTL constraint do not document border bargaining producing reciprocal help.
Calls to save the face do not show recruitment turning toward an offensive call.
The reasoned refusal answers a proposed expansion rather than an attack call.
Limiting a shift to avoid a fight does not establish an attack followed by border negotiations.
Mourning attributed destruction does not establish this room attacking and subsequently carrying a verbal contest.
The neighbouring plan and defensive call do not establish joining a coalition under attack.
Repeated canvas calls do not establish a subsequent host restriction on canvas talk.
Neither a bilateral agreement nor a representation dispute is established by the reported FTL preference.
Include prospective backup proposals while a face remains defendable, without assuming the backup was built or the existing spot abandoned.
A move can include renewed building immediately, as the mover reports starting a new face rather than merely selecting a location.
Include borrowing a plan from a neighbouring forum without inferring that its carrier negotiated for the room.
Include internally adjusting a border to reported neighbour intentions before treating the adjustment as a verified bilateral agreement.
Separate requesting scripts as a preparatory response to damage from evidence that scripts actually supplied placements.
Distinguish warnings relayed from other groups from announcements of chat decisions unless the decision, group membership and authority are evidenced.
Require evidence of a prior shared reference before reading jokes about current damage as inherited lore.
Include joking accounts of changed appearance alongside mourning and reports of damage.
Include disputes over the prank's expiry when a later reader rejects its April Fools timing and the maker insists it remains a joke.
